quote: As a woman, I have no country. As a woman I want no country. As a woman my country is the whole world.
source: Virginia Woolf, Three Guineas, section Three, on ‘our’ country (Hogarth Press, 1938) (the outsider)
speaker: the outsider
note: Corrected the locator. The sentences stand in section Three, a page before the Society of Outsiders is named, so that heading was too far on. Woolf puts the words inside quotation marks in the mouth of the outsider, answering a demand that she fight for her country, and the cut raises her lower case as to a capital.

evidence.where: the Project Gutenberg Australia text of Three Guineas, downloaded and searched directly; the passage sits after the section marker Three and before the first naming of the Society of Outsiders
evidence.edition: Three Guineas, Hogarth Press, 1938; written in English, so no translator
evidence.locator: section Three, inside the speech Woolf gives the outsider about ‘our’ country; the printed text reads in fact, as a woman, I have no country

reason: The wording is exact apart from the raised capital at the cut, and the comma after As a woman is Woolf’s own. The passage is in section Three but before the Outsiders’ Society is named, so the locator is tightened and the speaker is kept.
